entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance
entries.text: This document adds comparison evidence and acceptance tests. It does not replace or abbreviate Ideas.md, the glyph requirements, the MacFamilyTree walkthroughs, or the independent-feature contract. Competitor descriptions are observations, not proof of KinForge implementation. Official product pages were reviewed; this is not a hands-on examination of every competing product.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Primary Comparisons
entries.text:
| Product | Official evidence | What to evaluate in KinForge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MyHeritage | [Product overview](https://www.myheritage.com/help/en/articles/12852500-what-is-myheritage) describes tree building, historical research and DNA services. MyHeritage product material also emphasizes Record Matches, Smart Matches, Instant Discoveries, Record Detective, DNA matching and ethnicity tools, photo tools and Family Tree Builder. | Keep the original Markdown's complete matching, discovery, media and DNA scope. Evaluate actual evidence review and results rather than adopting provider names or claiming access to its collections. A local KinForge substitute must be a working record/research/matching workflow with visible evidence, confidence, review, attachment and undo; a generic search box or provider link is not parity. |
| MacFamilyTree 11 | [Version 11 features](https://www.syniumsoftware.com/macfamilytree/whatsnew) include photo processing, source/place customization, offline place lookup and website generation. | Compare inspector editing, traceable citations, real place data, independent chart behavior and configurable publication. Existing local walkthrough documents remain additional evidence; this web review is not a new installed-app walkthrough. |
| Ancestry | [Tree navigation documentation](https://help.ancestry.com/hc/en-us/articles/53933347829779-Navigating-an-Ancestry-Family-Tree) describes different tree views and media/search navigation. [Tree overview](https://www.ancestry.com/c/family-tree) describes building trees and importing GEDCOM. | Test continuity between chart, person profile, life events, media and attached evidence, alongside all the additional Ancestry-derived requirements already in Ideas.md. |

entries.text: These are reference products, not required connectors, services or purchases.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Additional Comparisons

| Product | Official evidence | KinForge acceptance focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RootsMagic | [Product overview](https://www.rootsmagic.com/RootsMagic) describes genealogy organization, research and publishing on Mac and Windows. | Data entry, evidence organization, portability and matching behavior across both desktop platforms. |
| Family Tree Maker | [Product features](https://www2.mackiev.com/ftm/index.html) describe change rollback, branch colors, charts and relative review. | Reversible edits, meaningful color coding, reviewable family contributions and recovery. Do not substitute a cloud subscription for an owned feature. |
| Family Historian | [Official help contents](https://www.family-historian.co.uk/help/fh7/hh_toc.htm) include property editing, nontraditional family relationships, source citations and record correction. | Precise relationship semantics, useful editing panes and citations that survive corrections. |
| Reunion | [Reunion 14 features](https://www.leisterpro.com/doc/v14/newfeatures/new14features.php) include event-linked media, custom report sections, note editing, chart tools and GEDCOM 7/GEDZIP. | Real media attachments, independent editable report sections, chart navigation and verified interchange. |
| Gramps | [Feature overview](https://blog.gramps-project.org/wiki/index.php/Features) describes dedicated people, family, event, place, citation, repository, media and note views. | Distinct workspaces with bidirectional links rather than one generic form reused under different names. |
| webtrees | [Features](https://webtrees.net/features/) describe collaboration and privacy at site, tree, user, record and fact levels. | Permission tests for specific records and sensitive facts, not merely a public/private label. |
| GenoPro | [Product overview](https://genopro.com/) describes genograms, contextual family editing, medical/criminal history panels and issue detection. | Relationship-symbol clarity and optional private annotations. Never infer a diagnosis or expose sensitive information through a glyph. |
| Legacy Family Tree | [Official tips and how-tos](https://legacyfamilytree.com/help/en/collections/17871831-tips-and-how-tos) cover backup restoration, additional parents, duplicate work, media handling and split views. | Actual recovery, complex families, comparison before merging and correct media references. |
| Heredis | [Product page](https://www.heredis.com/en/) describes family-tree software with tree, research, sources, maps, reports and publishing workflows. | Treat as a check on ergonomics: fast entry, guided research, maps, publishing and clear source traceability must be independently usable in KinForge. |
| Gramps Web | [Project site](https://www.grampsweb.org/) describes browser-based collaboration around Gramps genealogy data. | Collaboration, permissions and webapp behavior require real account/role tests, not just a local sign-in screen. |
| FamilySearch Family Tree | [Family Tree product page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/family-tree/) describes a shared collaborative family tree and record discovery. | Because the newest instruction says no connector/external service, KinForge must not fake FamilySearch integration; it can only provide local research tasks, reviewed citations, GEDCOM import/export and user-managed evidence unless a future connector is explicitly approved. |

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Competitor-Derived Working Feature Themes
entries.text: These themes consolidate MyHeritage, MacFamilyTree 11, Ancestry and the additional competitor review into testable KinForge behavior. They must be checked against the exact Markdown requirements, not used to replace them.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Competitor-Derived Working Feature Themes
entries.text:
| Theme | Required KinForge behavior | Not acceptable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic tree editing | Add parents before and after, add spouses/partners/children/siblings, keep siblings side by side, place descendants under prior generations, branch children from the couple line, and keep relationship names on person cards or legends rather than on connector labels. | Static screenshot, linear list, or lines with relationship text in the middle. |
| Evidence and hints | Local research assistant proposes missing-data questions, lets the user attach records/sources, preserves citations, shows confidence/notes, and keeps changes reversible. | Provider logos, external search links, unreviewed auto-merge, or sample-only discoveries. |
| Charts and reports | Every named chart/list/report in Ideas.md needs its own active generator path, editable draft, export path and verification. Reports with glyphs must label glyph meanings. | Multiple names pointing to the same generic page without distinct content or export validation. |
| Media | Photos, documents, PDFs, audio, video and web references must attach to people/families/sources/places/events, persist after reload and appear in relevant reports when requested. | Text-only "media note" standing in for real inserted images/PDFs. |
| Privacy and collaboration | Living/private data settings must alter exported files and shared views; account controls must persist user state and refuse invalid input. | Cosmetic lock labels or a local sign-in form that does not affect access behavior. |
| DNA and health/access annotations | DNA tools must expose recorded segment data, matching notes, side filters and citations without pretending to perform lab work. Disability/access glyphs must be user-authored, private by default and always labelled in trees/reports/charts. | Automatic diagnosis, ethnicity claims without data, or unlabeled sensitive glyphs. |
| Native and publish output | Web/webapp/native packaging controls must produce tangible files or navigable output; Mac/Windows packages must be validated separately and signing/notarization status must be stated. | Alerts telling the user to run a command, broken download buttons, or claiming pure Cocoa when the build is Electron. |

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Current 1.1.3 Control Correction
entries.text: The Publish page's Mac App card previously opened an instruction alert. That did not meet the working-control gate. In 1.1.3 source, it downloads `KinForge-mac-release-instructions.txt` with concrete build targets and acceptance checks, so the control has an observable result even though packaging still occurs outside the browser at build time.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Current 1.1.3 Control Correction
entries.text: The acceptance focus column is our design inference from these sources, not a claim that KinForge already matches or surpasses the product. Proprietary artwork, collections and branding are not being copied.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Exact-Requirement Rule
entries.text: The source register retains original passages, source line ranges and SHA-256 hashes. Its indexed content-block count is not a completed-feature count or a count of atomic requirements. Each compound passage still needs individual acceptance cases for every behavior it contains.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Exact-Requirement Rule
entries.text: An implementation must retain the original passage alongside its test cases. Similar wording or a working button is not sufficient. Examples from Ideas.md:

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Exact-Requirement Rule
entries.text:
| Exact source text | Required verification | Current boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Add PDFs or images" | Insert real content into an editable report; verify output and reopen. | The existing Add Media/PDF Note control inserts text only. Requirement unfinished. |
| "Unlimited undo & redo" | No arbitrary product history limit; reversible operations and recoverable resource exhaustion. | General history currently retains 50 states. Literal requirement not fulfilled. |
| "Optimize media" | Actual media processing with original retention, measured output and restoration. | Tag cleanup is now named Clean media tags. It is not media optimization. |
| "Search & replace, including nested hierarchical queries" | Review matching records, scope the tree, apply exact changes, undo, and test nested queries. | Literal text replacement is implemented with preview; nested queries remain unfinished. |
| "Developed in pure, native Cocoa" | A Cocoa implementation, not an Electron wrapper. | The current Mac preview uses Electron. It does not satisfy this literal technology requirement. |
| "Full FamilySearch integration (optional)" | Actual supported remote integration if enabled. | Conflicts with the newer no-connector instruction. Local research does not silently count as remote integration. |

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Exact-Requirement Rule
entries.text: Other provider-specific hosting, live institutional synchronization and external database claims have the same explicit conflict boundary. Software alone cannot provide cheek-swab/saliva laboratory processing, and an owned searchable record collection requires lawful data acquisition. Preserve these requirements, but do not mark an incompatible substitute complete.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Every command needs an observable outcome, appropriate validation, an error/retry path, persistence where relevant and an outcome-based test. The shared Button component now requires an action handler. That prevents one class of inert buttons; it is not proof of correct behavior.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: A missing implementation must not be disguised as a permanently disabled control, an external link, a success message, sample data or an unrelated action.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Temporary unavailability is legitimate only when required by state, such as Undo before any change or importing before a valid preview. Tests must also reach a valid state and activate the control.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Export tests must inspect the downloaded content, not just the download event.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Save tests must reopen data and compare meaningful fields, relationships and attachments.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Editor tests must cancel, apply, undo/redo where supported, and check other trees remain unchanged.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Empty-result actions must report that no changes were needed, without creating a false change-history entry.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Working-Control Gate
entries.text: Privacy tests must inspect the exported or shared data, not just the setting on screen.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: The earlier maintenance implementation iterated through all trees, parsed ambiguous dates through JavaScript Date, removed people without examining all their data, and labelled tag cleanup Optimize media. The 1.1.2 source replaces those actions with a reviewable plan scoped to the active tree.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Preview is read-only. Apply is explicit, and Cancel changes nothing.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: A stale preview cannot overwrite edits made after it was prepared.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Literal replacement preserves punctuation and replacement dollar signs.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Date normalization only reformats valid year-first numeric dates. Ambiguous dates, date qualifiers and invalid dates are preserved; this is not full genealogical date correction.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Name spacing is cleaned without changing cultural capitalization.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Only entirely empty, unreferenced people can be removed. Linked people, notes, sensitive details, access-needs data and events are preserved.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Family cleanup removes missing, repeated and cross-tree member references; it does not infer parentage or resolve all mismatched partnerships.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Undo and Redo are available in Maintenance. The existing 50-state limit remains a separate unfinished requirement.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Tag cleanup has its own accurate name. The original optimization requirement remains in the source register.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Concrete Maintenance Correction
entries.text: Evidence entry points: src/maintenance.test.ts, tests/browser/maintenance.spec.ts and tests/native-smoke.mjs. Actual pass/fail results belong to the test run and release Verification.json; the existence of these tests does not certify the entire product.

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Outstanding Control and Feature Audit
entries.text: The following are confirmed gaps or areas requiring deeper validation, not completed work:

entries.section: KinForge: Competitors and Working-Control Acceptance / Outstanding Control and Feature Audit
entries.text:
| Area | Observed boundary / remaining acceptance work |
| --- | --- |
| Charts | Many named choices still share a simplified rendering path. Verify every named layout, independent customization, saved positioning, pagination and real output. |
| Reports | Named templates require independent field/content checks; media-note text is not embedding. Verify editable exports and person-specific regeneration. |
| DNA | Add Segment inserts preset coordinates. Sorting shared cM is not genetic clustering, phasing, ethnicity inference or scientifically validated matching. |
| Media | Rotate, Warm tone and Contrast are basic display adjustments. Local crop, repair, ML colorization, transcription, scanning, recording and animation need their actual implementations and saved derivatives. |
| Maps and places | Place fields and decorative globe/map views are not a real offline globe, statistical map or sufficiently broad gazetteer. |
| Templates | Template names and generic fields do not establish 100 distinct, useful source templates or exact citation formatting. |
| Accounts | Local prototype login and password reset do not establish secure multi-user authentication, ownership, recovery or collaboration. Do not use the preview for sensitive production records. |
| Merging | Merge First Duplicate needs a field comparison, user resolution of conflicts and complete reference-preservation tests. |
| GEDCOM | Verify each requested encoding, version, subset, media reference, privacy rule and round trip. A small parser test set is not full standards coverage. |
| Research | Local archive search and reviewed links are a working subset. Licensed datasets, explainable hints, cross-tree discoveries, relationship theories and notifications remain separate work. |
| Platform delivery | Mac package checks do not certify Windows installation, live website deployment, every PWA/browser, Intel hardware or a pure Cocoa implementation. |
| Accessibility and scale | Per-person optional annotations are not a full accessibility audit. Test keyboard access, assistive technologies, supported languages and realistic large trees. |

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Catalogue
entries.text: This is an initial extensible catalogue, not a complete medical classification. Search aliases are discovery terms, not a statement that all matched labels are clinically equivalent. Related categories remain separate entries; selecting a search result never adds any other condition.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: These are labelled KinForge pictograms, not standardized diagnostic symbols. Small modifiers must not be used without their text label or an accessible equivalent.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: Every person can have multiple separately recorded disability entries. Adding cerebral palsy does not add paralysis, an intellectual disability, wheelchair use, or any access requirement.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: Disability records and access preferences have separate picker categories and profile groups. Neither is derived from the other.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: The user can preserve preferred identity wording, such as Deaf, or qualify an uncertain historical record, such as Possible CP - unconfirmed, using the editable Record label.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: Details and optional source links carry specifics such as affected areas, side, historical wording or uncertainty. The icon does not encode an unrecorded severity, cause, permanence or ability.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: The previous general disability entry and all existing access-needs IDs remain valid. Unrecognized imported glyph IDs keep their recorded text under Other annotations.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Design and Meaning
entries.text: Vector art uses licensed Lucide pictograms and small compositions of those pictograms, with the same rounded-line treatment as the rest of the KinForge set. The app and SVG export share one artwork renderer.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Privacy and Verification
entries.text: All new entries are private. Existing public-facing export paths omit them; full backups retain them. The local workspace and backups are not encrypted by this feature. No personal medical information was uploaded or published.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Privacy and Verification
entries.text: 31 automated tests passed, including 7 added for this clarification. The local production build passed. Browser checks covered category separation, CP and amputee search, a custom-label save/reload/edit cycle, an independent captions entry, mobile layout and visible Save/Cancel controls. Test-only records were cleared.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Privacy and Verification
entries.text: The live website, native installers and chart-level disability badges were not updated or released in this pass. No clinical validation or comprehensive assistive-technology audit is claimed.

entries.section: KinForge: Disability-Specific Glyphs / Terminology References
entries.text: The CP expansion was checked against [NINDS: Cerebral Palsy](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/cerebral-palsy). The decision to keep individual needs separate from broad disability labels is consistent with the diversity described in [WHO: Disability](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/disability-and-health). These sources do not endorse or supply the KinForge glyph designs.

entries.section: KinForge Glyph System
entries.text: Created 23 September 2026. This delivers a local glyph library and its integration into individual profiles. It does not complete the full Ideas.md application requirements or constitute a new published/native release.

entries.section: KinForge Glyph System / Design
entries.text: 67 glyph definitions: 8 relationship events, 17 other life-event/fallback glyphs, 17 disability categories, 22 access-needs categories and 3 record-status glyphs.

entries.section: KinForge Glyph System / Design
entries.text: 24-unit view boxes, 1.65-unit rounded strokes, unfilled line art and inherited text color. The preview supports 16-40 px sizes and light/dark appearances.

entries.section: KinForge Glyph System / Design
entries.text: Inspired by the compact, labelled pictograms observed in MacFamilyTree. KinForge's mappings and presentation are its own; the actual vector artwork uses the existing Lucide library under its included licence. No MacFamilyTree artwork was extracted or copied.

entries.section: KinForge Glyph System / Design

entries.section: KinForge: Complete Scope and Independent Implementation Contract / Owned Replacements
entries.text:
| Referenced capability | Required KinForge implementation | Completion boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FamilySearch / multi-site research | Local record catalogue, import, indexing, source comparison, reviewable hints and cross-tree matching over available data | An external search URL is not research implementation. Literal remote synchronization is incompatible with no connectors and remains a recorded conflict. |
| LDS ordinance sync | Private local ordinance records, dates, evidence, permissions and transfer within KinForge | Local tracking cannot confirm or update an outside institution's official records without that institution. |
| Wikipedia articles and images | Bundled/importable place-reference library with provenance, attribution and offline media | A title field or link is not a reference library; sufficient distributable content is still needed. |
| Historical record collections | KinForge-owned searchable collections populated with user-owned, public-domain or properly licensed material | Do not invent records, claim billions of holdings or copy restricted provider collections. Dataset acquisition is a separate deliverable. |
| Smart/record matches and discovery groups | Explainable local matching with evidence review and explicit acceptance before changes | Duplicate-name matching alone is not full record matching or validated family discovery. |
| Relationship theories | Graph-based candidate paths using documented sources, uncertainty and user review | Do not present inferred parentage as fact or a graph connection as proof of genetics. |
| DNA match/segment tools | Local file parsing, segment validation, chromosome views, supported matching/clustering and evidence-linked analysis | Displaying typed ethnicity labels or sorting cM values does not establish inference capability. |
| Ethnicity, genetic groups, journeys, traits and parental phasing | Scientifically validated local methods with appropriate reference data, uncertainty and applicability limits | Reference panels and validation remain required. Physical cheek-swab/saliva collection and laboratory genotyping cannot be supplied by software alone. Retain that literal conflict openly. |
| AI photo colorization, repair and enhancement | Actual local model inference with originals, previews, cancellation and saved derivatives | CSS sepia/contrast and no-op buttons are not machine learning or damage repair. |
| Face/whole-photo animation | Local processing with consent/provenance and clearly synthetic output | A story text field or static preview is not video generation. |
| Printed/handwritten transcription | Local OCR/handwriting models, language support, uncertainty and reviewed text | A manually editable transcription field is not OCR. |
| Maps, globe, statistics and gazetteer | Bundled map geometry, sufficiently broad place data and local calculation/rendering | Coordinate fields or dots on a decorative circle are not a complete globe/gazetteer. |
| Accounts, collaboration, messaging and notifications | Secure KinForge-owned identity, authorization, recovery, conflict handling and communications | Hosting decision pending user answer. Until resolved, do not assume a third-party identity/email/messaging service. Local profiles alone are not multi-user security. |
| Publication | Local document/book/website generation, privacy preview and portable export | No mandatory MacFamilyTree hosting, FTP provider or external publication account. A public site still needs a delivery host chosen separately. |
| Education | Original or distributable built-in research lessons and reference material | Links to paid webinars are not included educational content. |

entries.section: KinForge: Generations and Kinship Reports / Acceptance Criteria
entries.text: Calculate direct ancestors, descendants, siblings, aunts/uncles, nieces/nephews and cousins. Cousin degree is the smaller generation distance to a closest shared ancestor minus one; removal is the difference between the distances.

entries.section: KinForge: Generations and Kinship Reports / Acceptance Criteria

entries.section: KinForge: Generations and Kinship Reports / Acceptance Criteria

entries.section: KinForge: Generations and Kinship Reports / Acceptance Criteria
entries.text: Keep spouse, partner, guardian and independently recorded sibling relationships separate from calculated ancestry. A social connection is not proof of ancestry. Do not claim full/half sibling or biological status from incomplete parent records.

entries.section: KinForge: Generations and Kinship Reports / Acceptance Criteria
entries.text: Detect reachable ancestry cycles and report them without inventing results. Exclude cross-tree links and missing people. No recorded connection is not proof that people are unrelated.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Person, Family and Kinship Reports: formal write-ups for an individual, household or relationship line; narrative reports in continuous readable prose; particularities and person analysis highlighting unusual details or patterns.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Plausibility and Data Quality Reports: date and relationship consistency checks before publication; a source list compiling citations and distinguishing evidence from unsubstantiated claims.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Lists and Reference Reports: descendancy and marriage lists; places, events and anniversaries; Ahnentafel and genogram; timeline and name distribution; sociogram and influential people analysis.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Chart and Diagram Reports: fan, hourglass and relationship charts; Ahnentafel and genogram diagrams; timeline and name distribution charts.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Reports include the person's profile picture. The editable report behaves like a filled-in form, retaining the page design while values are edited.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Person and Kinship reports explain named first, second, third and later cousin relationships, including once, twice, thrice and later removals, and distinguish cousin-in-law connections.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Latest layout clarification: below the portrait/title header, section bands and body details return to the same left edge, without extra indentation. Latest type-size clarification: default report text is 15 pt, including header facts and explanations; section headings stay bold. This intentionally enlarges the compact type seen in the MacFamilyTree reference.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Corresponding MacFamilyTree 11 report content/features must be implemented, not just their titles. See KinForge-Report-Content-Parity.md for the manual-based comparison and explicit unfinished work.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / User's Requested Reports
entries.text: Every included glyph must have its meaning labelled beneath it, or explained in a report key. This applies to person cards, family trees, report charts, kinship reports and exports. Private annotations remain opt-in.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: These are built-in calculations over the user's recorded data. No provider is contacted to generate a report.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Ahnentafel cannot assign conventional paternal/maternal slot numbers when parent roles are unspecified. It lists those links instead of guessing from gender.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Fan images show at most five ancestor generations for readability; the other generation-limited reports allow up to ten. Large static diagrams are accompanied by their textual data.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Genogram symbols use recorded gender and relationship status, not inferred biological sex or medical conditions. Sociograms include only the relationship types currently stored by KinForge, not unrecorded friendships.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Influential people analysis is explicitly connection centrality, not a claim of historical influence. Missing evidence is not automatically speculation or falsehood.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: The formatted draft is a continuous editing surface, paginated for export/printing, not MacFamilyTree's full free-positioned layout engine. Embedded charts are regenerated snapshots, not individually draggable objects inside the document. A fillable PDF form with AcroForm fields is not implemented; the in-app draft fields are editable.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: RTF preserves basic text formatting and embedded images but reflows header columns. Text/CSV cannot contain photographs. External or SVG image URLs are not inserted into reports.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Downloaded PDFs use high-resolution rendered pages to preserve the editable report's exact visual layout and fonts. They are image-based, not searchable text or AcroForm documents. Browser Print can create a text-based PDF; Text and RTF remain available for text reuse. Export renders one page at a time to avoid oversized full-document canvases.

entries.section: KinForge Report Catalogue Requirements / Boundaries
entries.text: Existing other report menu entries outside this requested catalogue retain their prior limitations. This change does not certify every feature in Ideas.md or every report option in MacFamilyTree.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Reference and Scope
entries.text: Reference: [Synium's official MacFamilyTree 11.1 English manual](https://download.syniumsoftware.com/Manuals/MacFamilyTree_11.1_EN.pdf), printed pages 374-414. The manual was inspected locally, including rendered report and editing examples. This is not a claim of a fresh live walkthrough of the installed Mac app.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Reference and Scope
entries.text: The independent KinForge generators use local records and local rendering. No provider account, connector, remote medical inference or external report-generation service is used. The expanded implementations below close the earlier missing report generators and many editing/export gaps. They do not establish identical proprietary datasets, every native interaction, or pixel-identical parity.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Content Matrix
entries.text:
| Corresponding report | Implemented and testable locally | Remaining equivalence gaps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Person, pp. 374-375 | Names, events, pictures, facts, unions/offspring, explicit parentage, independently limited ancestor/descendant generations, narrative, hourglass, kinships, lifetime history, citations, profile photo and section selection | History catalogue is finite; no assertion that every proprietary field is replicated |
| Person Events, p. 376 | Person/immediate-family/all-relatives scope, event types, date intervals, lifetime filtering and unknown bounds | Approximate dates without a bounded interval do not acquire invented precision |
| Kinship, p. 377 | Maternal/paternal roles, named cousin degree/removal explanations, cousin-in-law distinction, symbols, relationship-category and parentage filters | Does not enumerate every longer path in pedigree-collapse families |
| Ahnentafel, p. 378 | Numbered mother/father slots, repeated ancestors, narratives including unnumbered ambiguous ancestors, parentage scope | Ambiguous parent roles are disclosed rather than assigned artificial numbers |
| Timeline, p. 379 | Chronological text/chart, recorded events and optional cited lifetime history | Independent chart styling; not every Mac template |
| Family, p. 380 | Family membership, unions, offspring, events, hourglass, citations and section selection | Local evidence only; unknown family facts are not inferred |
| Descendancy/Register, pp. 381-382 | Partners, descent paths, generation groups, continuation numbers, Roman child numbers and translated prose | Independent numbering implementation; unusual cyclic data is bounded |
| Map, p. 383 | Offline Natural Earth/D3 map, recorded coordinates, numbered place legend, events, citations, conservative chronological connections and missing-coordinate list | Contemporary generalized 1:110m land; no roads, historical borders or automatic geocoding |
| Narrative, p. 384 | Recorded life/family/event prose in 15 selectable languages and optional history | User text, stable headings and supplemental labels are not automatically translated |
| Today, p. 385 | Recurring Gregorian month/day calendar using parsed original dates | No current-year lunar/religious observance calculation |
| Status, p. 386 | Privacy-scoped entity counts, linked/unassigned media options and source counts | No external database statistics |
| Saved Reports, p. 387 | Restore content, report/list mode, generation options and presentation; rename/delete, undo; separate from original people | Old drafts remain unchanged until explicitly regenerated |
| Story, p. 388 | Documentary, album and chronicle templates, local photos/captions, narrative, citations, glyph meanings and page breaks | No proprietary Mac artwork/templates bundled |
| Persons/Marriages/Events/Facts/Places/Sources, pp. 390-395 | Configurable columns, sorting/grouping, event types/date filters, places, citations and uncited claims | Options are scoped to generators where they have an effect |
| ToDo/Anniversaries, pp. 396-397 | Task status filter, priority, sorted/grouped lists and month/day anniversary calendar | Gregorian recurrence only |
| Plausibility, p. 398 | Date intervals, parent/marriage/lifespan thresholds, cycles, duplicates, missing evidence and burial delay checks | A warning is not proof of error; unknown dates are not guessed |
| Distinctive Persons, p. 399 | Configurable child-count, early-death, marriage/parent-age and lifespan thresholds with bounded-date analysis | Unbounded ABT/CAL/EST values cannot establish exact ages |
| Analysis, p. 400 | Fact/event/person axes, counts, distributions, statistical summaries and local bar models | Not a statistical inference or causal-analysis service |
| Changes/LDS, pp. 401-402 | Local change log and explicit LDS fact types for baptism, confirmation, initiatory, endowment and sealings | No external ordinance registry; user date/status/temple text retained as recorded |
| Report editor, pp. 406-414 | Form-like editable fields, text formatting, image dimensions/alt/alignment, block multiselect/reorder, optional free-position X/Y/width/layer controls and multi-object drag, themes, crests, watermark, orientation/margins, header/footer/page numbers and explicit page breaks | Continuous onscreen preview rather than automatically paginated sheets; no chart-internal object editor claim; free-position placement retained in PDF/HTML, not plain text/CSV/RTF |
| Exports | Searchable Unicode hybrid PDF, genuine fillable AcroForm PDF, styled HTML/RTF, plain text/CSV, browser print and capability-based sharing | PDF visuals use local raster rendering plus text/widgets; native sharing varies by host |
| Family Tree Book / World History | Illustrated privacy-scoped person chapters, numbered contents, chapter citations/breaks; cited local and bundled historical context | Contents use chapter numbers, not computed page-number TOC; bundled history contains eight entries from 1776-1993, extensible through local dated/cited records |

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Date and Language Boundaries
entries.text: Original date text and GEDCOM qualifiers are preserved. Explicit Julian, Hebrew, historical French Revolutionary and arithmetic Islamic dates can be converted for chronological comparisons using a local calendar library. Unlabelled dates are not guessed to use another calendar.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Date and Language Boundaries
entries.text: French Revolutionary conversion is restricted to historical years 1-14. Arithmetic Islamic conversion is not an observed lunar calendar. Anniversary recurrence is Gregorian, not a prediction of religious observances.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Date and Language Boundaries
entries.text: Narrative languages: English, German, Danish, French, Finnish, Italian, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Hungarian, Polish, Norwegian Bokmal and Czech. Generated sentence templates are translated; user-authored facts and citations are never rewritten by a translation service.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Date and Language Boundaries
entries.text: Parentage is explicitly recorded as unspecified, biological, adoptive, foster or step. Missing parentage is never silently treated as biological. Existing links and new parent/child controls can edit this value.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Person symbols use one shared definition catalogue. The family tree captions sit directly beneath icons; a fixed-height scrollable annotation area prevents long lists moving family connectors.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Private disability/access-needs annotations require the explicit tree toggle or report private-data option. No condition is inferred from gender, a relationship, an access request or a different diagnosis.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Reports show the glyph, caption and full meaning. A custom record label is preserved alongside the catalogue meaning and recorded details.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Network diagrams include captioned symbols in the person card. Up to three are shown in a compact diagram card; the person's complete labelled key follows the chart. A visible note points to additional symbols when necessary.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Genogram shapes are labelled on the person card and explained in the report. Relationship line samples are paired with meanings. Separation, divorce and annulment marks are distinguished explicitly. Connection text remains off the tree connectors.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: Kinship reports attach meanings to the reference person and each displayed relative, including when names are duplicated. Private profiles receive no identifying symbol detail unless included.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: PDF/RTF include embedded bitmaps and captions. Text/CSV retain the caption and explanation but cannot contain an image. User-edited drafts are not silently rewritten; regenerate a new draft to receive new generated content.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Symbol Contract
entries.text: PDFs include searchable Unicode text over the rendered page. The separate fillable PDF action exports real AcroForm fields with editable values and Unicode appearances. Original SVG input is not accepted; trusted internal library symbols are rasterized locally before insertion.

entries.section: KinForge Report Content and Symbol Acceptance Checklist / Verification

Browser suites exercise report editing, rich reports, parentage/history entry and downloaded PDF validation. These checks cover specified local behaviour, not every Ideas.md feature or every Mac interaction.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout
entries.text: Requested 23 September 2026. Implemented in the 1.1.3 development preview's dynamic Family Tree workspace.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: "IT should be grouped by family, so meaning if this child has children, and a husband, then the descendatns and children should branch out from the line that connects the couple to below, the word sibling or spouse, or etc, shouldn't be in the middle of both people cards, and should not be the thing connecting both individuals, it should be a line, however, I also want there to be a legend  to show what each line represents"

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: The user's latest message requests a visible legend, superseding the preceding request for a QR code. No QR code or external legend service is needed.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Group each sibling with their own spouse or partner, including when the partner was entered later.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Join a couple with a line, and branch their recorded shared children downward from a junction on that line.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Use one child bar for siblings who have the same recorded parent set, with individual stems to their cards.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Apply the same structure recursively to subsequent generations.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Do not place relationship words between the person cards. Accessible descriptions remain available to assistive technology, and the inspector retains relationship names.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Keep a visible legend outside the chart so it does not cover people or connectors. Show line samples for spouses, partners, parents and children, separately recorded siblings, co-parents without a recorded union, and guardianship.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Reflect explicitly stored separation, divorce and annulment statuses with marks on the union line and matching legend entries. Do not infer these statuses from other facts.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Preserve single-parent and half-sibling records. A spouse or partner is not automatically a recorded parent.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Provide Spouse and Other parent choices in Add relative. Creating a child with two selected parents is one undoable action.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Recalculate connections after adding or unlinking relationships, moving cards, undoing, redoing or reloading. No external service is used.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Family Group Follow-Up
entries.text: Tests are in src/familyLines.test.ts, src/treeGraph.test.ts, tests/browser/generations.spec.ts and tests/native-smoke.mjs. Browser checks include separate sibling couples, shared child bars, single-parent preservation, two-parent creation and undo/redo, visible legend entries, no edge text labels, connector/card intersections, mobile layout and persistence.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: Latest centring clarification: "So when the line comes down, it's supposed to be centre, and then branch out, into different branches on the left or right, so branch out on the left or on the right, if there is more than one children connected to the parents"

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: The downward stem meets the centre of the children's horizontal branch, midway between its outermost child connections.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: Two children branch left and right from that central stem. Three children can have left, centre and right stems.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: In the ordinary shared-parent layout, the stem drops straight from the couple midpoint to this centred branch.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: Solve card positions and branch centres together, including mixed-parent families and moved cards. Do not use a sideways elbow as the normal solution to an offset. This supersedes the earlier intermediate elbow workaround.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: The screenshot clarification is the regression baseline: "If there is two children, the line should be at the centre, so one on the right or on the left, that's why it's called da family tree as it looks like a tree, you can see the offests in this image".

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: Recreate all eleven people and fourteen relationships in that example. June and Taylor's midpoint must align with Lee and Lou's midpoint; Kai must align below June, Kit below Lee, and Sam below Robin and Morgan's midpoint. Do not invent missing parentage to obtain this layout.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: Check the rendered paths and node coordinates for two-child, three-child, mixed-parent and moved-card arrangements; keep the same behaviour in the Mac build.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Exact Request
entries.text: "IF the relatives are siblings, it should look like next to each other, if they are descendatns, and children, the children, and descendants, should go below the previous generation"

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Explicitly recorded siblings sit alongside one another on the same horizontal row, including when their parents have not been entered.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Children who share a recorded parent, including half siblings, are grouped on the same row.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Children appear below their parents; grandchildren and further descendants continue downward by generation.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Shorter branches and cousins retain their generation rather than being pushed down to the lowest descendant row.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Partners remain together when this does not contradict recorded ancestry. Parent-child direction takes precedence over impossible or cross-generation partner alignment.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: A sibling who is also a guardian remains in the sibling generation. A guardianship link does not invent biological parentage.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Dragging permits horizontal positioning while preserving generation rows and making room between cards.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Saved arrangements cannot restore incorrect vertical positions. Older layout caches, or caches for a different relationship structure, are recalculated; person records and relationships are not changed.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Layout Rules
entries.text: Arrange tree restores the relationship-based layout. The same generation constraints apply on desktop and mobile.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Evidence and Limits
entries.text: The implementation retains Dagre for graph ordering and uses a bundled, offline Cassowary solver for simultaneous family centring, card separation and generation constraints. It does not infer or save missing parent relationships merely to align siblings. Impossible imported arrangements retain non-overlapping cards and may need a connector bend; valid tested families have straight centred stems.

entries.section: KinForge: Siblings and Generation Layout / Evidence and Limits
entries.text: Tests are in src/treeGraph.test.ts, tests/browser/generations.spec.ts and tests/native-smoke.mjs. They check explicit siblings, shared-parent siblings, half siblings, uneven branches, cousins, guardian siblings, overlapping cards, saved positions, ancestor insertion and package execution.

entries.section: Complex Fictional Family Tree: Hands-On Exploration Guide / Import Boundaries
entries.text: The fixture uses GEDCOM 5.5.1 because that version was explicitly visible in the inspected MacFamilyTree export menu. Compatibility is still unverified until an actual import. The format's family-level pedigree values do not provide a standard `step` value or a complete modern relationship model. Therefore Ellis's intended step relationship is documented for native testing rather than falsely encoded as birth/adoption; Jules and Lee use person associations until their native family is created. These are fixture decisions based on the [GEDCOM 5.5.1 specification](https://gedcom.io/specifications/ged551.pdf), not claims that MacFamilyTree lacks those features.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: These are design and test targets, not newly completed implementation:

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Build distinct, connected workspaces rather than a single static page. Preserve tree/person/event/source identity across views.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Separate record editing from chart/document presentation. Both need explicit saved, unsaved and error states.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Support quick inline edits and full evidence editors that share the same records.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Treat sources as reusable records and citations as claim-specific evidence with locators, notes and certainty.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Model parentage per parent-child link, and relationship history as dated, sourced events.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Preserve uncertain and partial dates without inventing missing days or months.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Make maintenance changes previewable and reversible, with conflict review rather than silent merging.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Use clear privacy choices in every chart, report, export and publication path, especially for living people and sensitive attributes.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Validate data, visual rendering and persisted/exported output independently. A partially loaded map or a visible export button is not a passed workflow.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Feature Coverage and Deep-Inspection Ledger / 12. Lessons for KinForge
entries.text: Use an original, consistent glyph system with labels and accessible alternatives. Do not copy proprietary artwork or imply clinical meaning without user-provided data.

entries.text: Keep the supplied Ideas.md as the complete KinForge requirement baseline. This reference does not replace its custom features or establish web/PWA/DMG/EXE/website parity.

entries.text: This follow-up inspected the actual interface, not just the feature catalogue. Screenshots were viewed in the conversation; this Markdown file is the written reference, not a saved screenshot bundle. No record values, chart styling or report text were changed. entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 1. Chart Workspace and Element Inspector
entries.text: **Observed:** Fan-chart viewing has a central canvas, left navigation and a right person browser. Entering Edit changes the title to Edit Chart, presents a page canvas and exposes a Finish action. Selecting the center person replaces the empty right inspector with properties for that chart element.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 1. Chart Workspace and Element Inspector
entries.text: **Controls inspected:** Full Name; top/bottom margins; fill and border colors; border width; name and secondary fonts; text color; shadow opacity, distance, angle, blur and color; and checkboxes for which events, facts and influential relationships to display. The toolbar includes undo/redo, removal, front/back order, text, lines, images, alignment and realignment. Page setup and pagination controls are visible.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 1. Chart Workspace and Element Inspector
entries.text: **Health:** Selection-to-inspector behavior worked. Transformation, undo, pagination and export outcomes were not exercised. Some inspector values were truncated in narrow controls, and the name wrapped mid-word.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 1. Chart Workspace and Element Inspector
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Separate genealogical facts from presentation overrides. A person-selection editor changes records; a chart-element inspector changes presentation. Use readable fields, compact grouped controls and unmistakable mode labels.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 2. Report Workspace and Document Inspector
entries.text: **Observed:** A generated Person Report becomes an editable page in Edit Report mode. Clicking its heading visibly selects that text element and opens a different right-hand inspector appropriate to document layout.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 2. Report Workspace and Document Inspector
entries.text: **Controls inspected:** Font, style, size, text color, fitting width, horizontal/vertical alignment, line breaks, keeping an element with the preceding object, page breaks, background, border edges/radius, margins and padding. The Add menu offers Text, Image and PDF.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 2. Report Workspace and Document Inspector
entries.text: **Health:** Entering edit mode and selecting an element worked. No content was inserted or rewritten. Saving, regeneration semantics and editable export formats remain unverified.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 2. Report Workspace and Document Inspector
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Treat reports as structured documents with selection-aware formatting, not screenshots of a chart. Define clearly whether a saved report is a live template or a snapshot, and test what happens when its underlying records change.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 3. Person Profile and Form Mode
entries.text: **Observed:** The main person page shows identity and lifespan, parents above, a person browser on the right, and partner/children context along the bottom. Edit changes the page to form mode; Done provides an explicit way out. Empty optional sections become available in editing mode.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 3. Person Profile and Form Mode
entries.text: **Health:** The form-mode transition worked and the family context stayed visible. The large bottom context pane substantially reduced the visible form area. The fixed header and surrounding panes also consumed considerable vertical space.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 3. Person Profile and Form Mode
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Retain identity and nearby relationships while editing, with compact or collapsible context panes. Keep the active form's controls reachable without being covered by a floating pane. Use a searchable section list for long records.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 4. Inline Event Editing and Full Event Detail
entries.text: **Observed:** Selecting an existing census event expanded an inline editor with type, date, time, description, cause, authority, labels, privacy, notes, place and citation information. Edit Event Details opened a dedicated event page with sections for place, media, notes, citations, stories, tasks, labels and change dates, plus a Show Person action.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 4. Inline Event Editing and Full Event Detail
entries.text: **Health:** Both levels of detail opened successfully and retained the selected event. No values were submitted or changed.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 4. Inline Event Editing and Full Event Detail
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Provide quick edits in the person's timeline and a focused event editor for evidence-heavy work. Both must edit the same underlying event and preserve a clear route back to the person.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 5. Historical Date Precision
entries.text: **Observed:** The date selector has Full Date, Month & Year, Year Only and Date Range modes. The inspected sample retained a year-only value of 1930. Prefix/suffix menus expose uncertainty and qualification terms, including About, Before, After, estimated/calculated variants and multilingual alternatives. The dialog was cancelled without selecting a qualifier or altering the date.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 5. Historical Date Precision
entries.text: **Health:** The existing precision was represented explicitly. Parsing, calendar conversion, range validation and serialization were not tested.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 5. Historical Date Precision
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Store date precision and qualifiers explicitly. Do not turn an unknown day or month into an invented January 1 date. Sorting and plausibility rules must respect uncertain dates.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 6. Tree Selection and People Search
entries.text: **Observed:** In Interactive Tree, the right pane switches among Edit, Persons and Relatives. Searching for Rose Fitzgerald filtered the people list. Selecting her changed the tree title, selected node and displayed family structure. Selecting John Fitzgerald Kennedy through the relatives list returned the tree to him; the Edit pane then displayed his record. The zoom control was also exercised at a readable editing scale.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 6. Tree Selection and People Search
entries.text: **Health:** Search, selection, redraw and the contextual editor worked during this walkthrough. This was a small sample, not a large-tree performance test.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 6. Tree Selection and People Search
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Share a stable selected-person identifier across the tree, inspector, reports and research views. Search should locate a person without hiding or altering their family relationships. Preserve tree position sensibly when switching panes.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 7. Relatives Browser and Focus Context
entries.text: **Observed:** The Relatives pane grouped the focused person, partner and children. A Lock Focused Person control was visible. When a child was selected, the tree selection changed while the relatives browser still showed the previous person's family context. The lock itself was not toggled.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 7. Relatives Browser and Focus Context

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Interface and Editing-Pane Follow-Up / 7. Relatives Browser and Focus Context
entries.text: **KinForge inspiration:** Support an explicit relationship-reference person separately from the active selection when useful. Label both states and provide a clear recenter/reset action.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Walkthrough Steps
entries.text: **Person workspace: opened successfully.** Navigating from the Relationship Chart to Persons retained John Fitzgerald Kennedy. The citation's Edit button navigated to the underlying source page; it did not open a separate full-page citation editor in this flow. entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: The following are design targets derived from this pass, not newly implemented features:

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Keep navigation, the main workspace and its inspector distinct.** Use a stable left navigation area, a central tree/list/document, and a context-sensitive inspector where appropriate. A focused editor should be able to use more width when the work becomes evidence-heavy.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Keep identity visible without crowding the form.** Use a compact person/event heading and collapsible relationship context. Avoid oversized headings and persistent overlays consuming most of the editing viewport.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Provide two editing depths.** Quick inline changes and a dedicated editor must refer to the same record. The deeper editor should expose citations, media, notes and privacy without making common edits cumbersome.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Distinguish a source from its citation.** Store reusable source metadata separately from a citation's page locator, notes and certainty. Use explicit actions such as Open Source and Return to Event instead of an ambiguous Edit label that changes the record being viewed.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Make evidence navigation bidirectional.** Person -> event -> citation/source and source -> referenced event -> person should be traversable. Preserve selection, and intentionally restore scroll position or focus when returning.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Use preview panes for quick context.** Tree and timeline previews can avoid full-page navigation, but they must fit within the viewport and keep close/expand controls reachable. Offer a full view when the content needs more room.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Use icons with labels and clear states.** Section glyphs and event pictograms help scanning, but meaning must not depend on color alone. KinForge should keep its own licensed/original glyph system and branding rather than copy MacFamilyTree's artwork or exact visual skin.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Context Panes and Evidence Navigation Follow-Up / Interface Direction for KinForge
entries.text: **Adapt to the window.** On wide displays, allow useful side-by-side information. On compact displays or with enlarged text, switch to one active pane, retain a clear back action and prevent floating controls from covering form actions.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: These are implementation and acceptance-test targets, not claims that KinForge already meets them:

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Use one connected record model.** A selected person must connect consistently to relationships, events, facts, places, citations, media, stories and tasks across views.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Keep each major workflow distinct.** Tree exploration, structured editing, research, maps, chart composition, report editing and publication need appropriate screens while retaining person/tree context.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Implement genuinely different chart layouts.** Verify the geometry, branch selection, generation limits, repeated ancestors, names, privacy and export output for each required chart.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Separate sources from citations.** Reuse a source while allowing each factual assertion to have its own citation, locator, quotation and evidence assessment.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Make research questions actionable.** Link each question to missing or conflicting data; support answers, deferral and explicit unknown states without inventing family facts.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Make quality findings reviewable.** Show the relevant records and rationale. Account for approximate dates and relationship types, and never silently rewrite a user's tree.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Preserve original media.** Treat crop, color correction and AI transformations as distinct operations with previews and explicit save/revert behavior. A visible checkbox is not evidence that a transformation works.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Treat privacy as part of every workflow.** Private and living-person details must be tested across charts, reports, exports and sharing, not only the editor. DNA, government identifiers, custody/protective-services and criminal-history fields in Ideas.md need especially careful access and disclosure controls.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Test import/export round trips.** Verify relationships, events, citations, media references, dates, encodings and private-data exclusions with real fixtures. The export menu alone is not sufficient.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Read-Only Feature Walkthrough / Implications for KinForge
entries.text: **Do not confuse a provider template with a service.** Storing a DNA record or opening an external search does not deliver DNA analysis, private record access, automatic matching or licensed content.

entries.text: These are proposed acceptance criteria derived from observation. They have **not been implemented or tested by this research pass**.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Maintain separate categories for person notation, relationship notation, event icons, research/status badges and interface actions. Do not let a decorative style change alter the stored meaning of a record.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Provide an accessible, chart-specific legend. Show text labels or accessible names and tooltips, not color alone. Printed and exported charts need their own readable legend.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Keep the same event identity and recognizable icon across the person timeline, inline editor, full event editor, chart options and report output.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Use explicit labels for unknown, unrecorded and user-defined identity values. Do not assign an unverified shape or collapse distinct values just to match a competitor's menu.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Define and document each relationship connector before using it. Biological, adoptive, foster, guardian, step, partner and other supported links need data-model and rendering tests, not only different line styles.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Treat sensitive medical, DNA, government, custody and criminal-history annotations as controlled data. A symbol must not imply a diagnosis, legal finding or biological relationship unsupported by the record and evidence.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Support user-defined event types with a stable identifier, a name, an optional icon and a readable fallback. Preserve meaning when an icon is unavailable in an export or on another platform.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Use an independently designed or appropriately licensed icon set for KinForge. Study MacFamilyTree's conventions without copying its proprietary artwork or branding.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Test gender/person states, living/deceased markers, event types, custom-type fallback, chart selection and each relationship type independently. Include uncertain dates and conflicting evidence.

entries.section: MacFamilyTree 11: Symbol Reference for KinForge / 5. KinForge Design and Test Targets
entries.text: Test keyboard access, screen-reader names, enlarged text, high contrast, grayscale output, zoomed-out charts and mobile layouts. Check that marks remain legible without obscuring names or dates.

entries.section: KinForge Genealogy Studio 1.1.0 / Dynamic Family Workspace
entries.text: The application now opens on an interactive family chart. People, Families, Library, Research, Media, Charts, Reports, Places and Sources, DNA, publishing, maintenance and the dashboard have independent navigation addresses. Person profiles have separate overview, edit, timeline, source and media pages. Browser Back/Forward and refresh preserve the page and selected person.

entries.section: KinForge Genealogy Studio 1.1.0 / Dynamic Family Workspace
entries.text: The chart supports pan, zoom, fit-to-view, a minimap, draggable people, saved positions, automatic household layout, full-tree, ancestor and descendant views, and generation depth. Changes in the inspector or profile editor update the same family data. Relatives can be created or linked from existing people. Parent-child connections may also be drawn between node handles. Duplicate links, self-links, cross-tree links and circular ancestry are rejected. Unlinking a relationship keeps both people. Undo and redo are available during the session.

entries.section: KinForge Genealogy Studio 1.1.0 / Dynamic Family Workspace
entries.text: The People directory supports search by name, alias and label, birth-date or name sorting, and filters for living, private and unsourced people. Family groups derive from the recorded relationships. Switching trees resets the selected person to the destination tree.
